# `Q-22-1` — Unknown Math Command

> A `\command` in a math expression is not a known LaTeX math command and was not defined with `\newcommand` earlier in the same expression, so no writer can render it.

## What this means

Math is written in LaTeX syntax, and every `\name` must be a command quarto-math knows (the standard LaTeX and amsmath math commands, plus the macros the expression defines with `\newcommand`). This error fires when a command is neither. The diagnostic underlines the command; the rest of the expression is still parsed, but the whole equation is emitted verbatim as source text in formats that need a conversion (Word), because half-converted math would be worse than none.

## Why this happens

Common causes: a typo (`\aplha`), a command from a LaTeX package that has no math meaning (`\textsuperscript`), a document-level macro defined in a LaTeX preamble that this expression cannot see, or a control sequence that is not standard at all (`\R` for the reals).

## How to fix it

Fix the spelling, replace the command with its standard equivalent (`\mathbb{R}`), or define it in the expression: `\newcommand{\R}{\mathbb{R}} x \in \R`. HTML output through MathJax or KaTeX may still render an unknown macro if that engine defines it; this error is about the converters Quarto runs itself.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
